verdicts.rewritten_summary: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): the congressional Comision de Mujer y Familia approved by unanimity a dictamen merging bills 6506 and 8457 (sponsored by Jorge Montoya and Alejandro Munante) that would prohibit any person from entering public sanitary facilities designated for the sex opposite to their birth sex, with narrow exceptions (custody, and cases where required, including accompanying minors, the elderly or people with disabilities), and would oblige venues not to post ambiguous restroom signs; the article notes the text still needed plenary backing and reports the trigger as the July 2023 complaint over gendered restroom labels at Lima's Jorge Chavez international airport. Activist Gianna Camacho is quoted arguing the measure is discriminatory and that enforcement would rest on security staff checking the DNI to decide whether a woman entering a women's restroom is trans or cisgender. This is the national framework this department is scored against; the article contains no Lambayeque-specific content.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: IDEHPUCP legal analysis (15 April 2025, Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte): on Wednesday 2 April 2025 the plenary of Congress approved and waived a second vote on the dictamen of the 'Ley que fortalece el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los ninos y adolescentes', whose Article 5.1 prohibits persons from entering or using public sanitary facilities designated for a sex other than their birth sex. The institute reads Article 5 as a direct breach of equality and non-discrimination (Article 2(2) of the Peruvian Constitution and Article 1.1 of the American Convention on Human Rights), resting on the stereotype that trans people are more prone to enter restrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors, and recalls documented cases of trans people barred from public restrooms - including SPC-INDECOPI Resolution 0735-2022 dismissing a trans woman's discrimination complaint against SmartFit, where the company grounded bathroom assignment on the sex recorded in the DNI - and the fact that gender-identity recognition in Peru remains long, costly and invasive. This is the national framework this department is scored against; the article contains no Lambayeque-specific content.

The piece recounts the February 2023 murder of trans sex worker Rubi Torres Silvano (31), kidnapped from central Lima by a 'Los Gallegos' extortion gang and killed in Carabayllo with some 30 gunshots (Priscila Aguado Huatuco, 30, was shot days earlier), with two killers arrested in March 2023, and notes the state has not incorporated sexual orientation or gender identity into its crime-registration systems, so hate crimes cannot be prosecuted as such.
